text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use falls mostly on low-complexity patients, but the records sample is too thin to confirm or refute support for the billed level.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is concerning: 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with no chronic conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215s are dominated by simple presentations such as rash (C0025265, C0025385), low back pain (C0025592, C0026015) and UTI (C0026866, C0026898), where a highest-level visit would be unusual. Against that, the documentation does not show unsupported billing: the four documented 99215s (e.g., C0026003, C0026461) were reviewed at high MDM. But four claims out of 281, with only a small share of all claims reviewed, is far too few to judge. The few notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim are only weak evidence of cloned or inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts targeted at the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet. The check is whether MDM and time genuinely support level 5 for those encounters, and whether note text is templated across visits."}
